0.1.name: Northern
0.1.description: The more eastern of two similar features, or the eastern-most of several similar features.

0.2.name: South Eastern
0.2.description: The more south-eastern of two similar features, or the south-eastern-most of several similar features.

0.3.name: Upper
0.3.description: Where the control feature is directly above a similar feature.

0.4.name: Lower
0.4.description: Where the control feature is directly below a similar feature.

0.5.name: Middle
0.5.description: Where the control feature is the middle one of a number of similar features.

1.1.name: Terrace
1.1.description: A level area on a slope.

1.2.name: Spur
1.2.description: A contour projection or "nose" rising from the surrounding ground.

1.3.name: Re-entrant
1.3.description: A contour indentation; a valley; the opposite of a spur.

1.4.name: Earth Bank
1.4.description: An abrupt change in ground level which can clearly be distinguished from its surroundings.

1.5.name: Quarry
1.5.description: Gravel, sand or stone working in flat or inclined ground.

1.6.name: Earth Wall
1.6.description: A narrow wall of earth projecting above the surrounding terrain, may be partially stone-faced, usually man-made.

1.7.name: Erosion Gully
1.7.description: An erosion gully or trench, normally dry.

1.8.name: Small Erosion Gully
1.8.description: A small erosion gully or trench, normally dry.

1.9.name: Hill
1.9.description: A high point. Shown on the map with contour lines.

1.11.name: Saddle
1.11.description: The low point between two higher points.

1.12.name: Depression
1.12.description: A depression or hollow from which the ground rises on all sides. Shown on the map with contour lines.

1.13.name: Small Depression
1.13.description: A small, shallow, natural depression or hollow.

1.14.name: Pit
1.14.description: A pit or hole with distinct steep sides. Usually man-made.

1.15.name: Broken Ground
1.15.description: Clearly disturbed ground with features too small or too numerous to be mapped individually.

1.16.name: Ant Hill
1.16.description: The mound made by ants or termites.

2.1.name: Cliff, Crag
2.1.description: A cliff or rock face. May be passable or impassable.

2.3.name: Cave
2.3.description: A hole in a rock face or hill side, often leading to underground workings.

2.4.name: Boulder
2.4.description: A prominent free-standing block of rock or stone.

2.5.name: Boulder Field
2.5.description: An area covered with so many boulders that they cannot be mapped individually.

2.6.name: Boulder cluster
2.6.description: A compact group of closely spaced boulders.

2.7.name: Stony Ground
2.7.description: An area covered with many small stones or rocks.

2.8.name: Bare Rock
2.8.description: Exposed rock with little or no soil or vegetation cover.

2.9.name: Narrow Passage
2.9.description: A gap between two cliffs or rock faces that face each other.

3.1.name: Lake
3.1.description: A large body of water, normally shown as uncrossable.

3.2.name: Pond
3.2.description: A small body of water, sometimes seasonal or shallow.

3.3.name: Waterhole
3.3.description: A hollow or pit containing water.

3.5.name: Minor Water Channel
3.5.description: A small ditch or channel that may carry water intermittently.

3.6.name: Narrow marsh
3.6.description: A thin strip of marsh or wet ground.

3.7.name: Marsh
3.7.description: An area of wet ground with marsh vegetation.

3.8.name: Firm ground in marsh
3.8.description: A dry or firm patch within or between areas of marsh.

3.9.name: Well
3.9.description: A visible shaft or enclosed source containing water.

3.10.name: Spring
3.10.description: A distinct place where water emerges from the ground.

3.11.name: Water tank / trough
3.11.description: A constructed container used to hold water.

4.1.name: Open land
4.1.description: An area without tree cover, such as grassland or a field.

4.2.name: Semi-open land
4.2.description: Open ground with scattered trees or bushes.

4.3.name: Forest corner
4.3.description: A corner or tip of woodland projecting into open ground.

4.4.name: Clearing
4.4.description: A small open area surrounded by woodland.

4.5.name: Thicket
4.5.description: A dense group of vegetation that is difficult to pass through.

4.6.name: Linear thicket
4.6.description: A narrow line of dense trees or bushes, including a hedge.

4.7.name: Vegetation boundary
4.7.description: A distinct boundary between types of vegetation.

4.8.name: Copse
4.8.description: A small group of trees, or a more runnable patch inside denser woodland.

4.9.name: Prominent tree
4.9.description: An individual tree that is particularly distinctive.

4.10.name: Root Stock / Tree Stump
4.10.description: A prominent uprooted root system or tree stump.

5.1.name: Road
5.1.description: A surfaced or unsurfaced road suitable for ordinary vehicles.

5.2.name: Track / Path
5.2.description: A visible route made by people, animals or vehicles.

5.3.name: Ride
5.3.description: A cleared line through woodland without a distinct path.

5.4.name: Bridge
5.4.description: A structure crossing over water or another linear feature.

5.5.name: Power line
5.5.description: An overhead power or communication line, cableway or lift.

5.6.name: Pylon
5.6.description: A support for an overhead line, cableway or lift.

5.7.name: Tunnel
5.7.description: A passage underneath a road, railway or other feature.

5.8.name: Wall
5.8.description: A wall built from stone or another material.

5.9.name: Fence
5.9.description: A constructed boundary of wire, wood or similar material.

5.10.name: Crossing point
5.10.description: A gate, stile or other place to cross a linear barrier.

5.11.name: Building
5.11.description: A building or a pillar supporting a roof.

5.12.name: Paved area
5.12.description: An area with a hard surface, such as a car park.

5.13.name: Ruin
5.13.description: The remains of a damaged or collapsed building.

5.14.name: Prominent man-made line feature
5.14.description: A distinctive constructed linear feature, such as an above-ground pipeline.

5.15.name: Tower / Pylon
5.15.description: A tower or similar tall constructed structure.

5.16.name: Shooting platform
5.16.description: A raised observation or shooting platform attached to a tree.

5.17.name: Boundary stone / Cairn
5.17.description: A constructed stone marker or pile of stones.

5.18.name: Fodder rack
5.18.description: A structure used to provide feed for animals.

5.19.name: Charcoal burning ground / Platform
5.19.description: A former charcoal site or a small constructed level platform.

5.21.name: Canopy
5.21.description: A roofed area that can be entered or passed through.

5.22.name: Stairway
5.22.description: A staircase with at least two steps.

5.23.name: Out of Bounds area
5.23.description: A small area that must not be entered, such as a flower bed.

5.24.name: Railway / Tramway
5.24.description: A railway, tramway or similar railed track.

6.1.name: Special Item — Cross
6.1.description: A special feature whose meaning must be explained in the event information.

6.2.name: Special Item — Circle
6.2.description: A special feature whose meaning must be explained in the event information.

8.1.name: Low
8.1.description: Adds that a feature is particularly low or flat.

8.2.name: Shallow
8.2.description: Adds that a hollow or channel is particularly shallow.

8.3.name: Deep
8.3.description: Adds that a hollow or channel is particularly deep.

8.4.name: Overgrown
8.4.description: Adds that vegetation partly covers the feature.

8.5.name: Open
8.5.description: Adds that the surrounding tree cover is relatively open.

8.6.name: Rocky / Stony
8.6.description: Adds that the feature is rocky or surrounded by stones.

8.7.name: Marshy
8.7.description: Adds that the feature is in wet or marshy ground.

8.8.name: Sandy
8.8.description: Adds that the feature or surrounding ground is sandy.

8.11.name: Ruined
8.11.description: Adds that a constructed feature has fallen down or is damaged.

10.1.name: Crossing
10.1.description: Two linear features cross here. Identify the features in columns D and E.

10.2.name: Junction
10.2.description: Features meet here. Identify the two features in columns D and E.

11.1.name: Bend
11.1.description: A smooth change in the direction of a linear feature.

12.1.name: North East Side
12.1.description: The flag is outside the north-east side of the feature.

12.2.name: South East Edge
12.2.description: The flag is at the south-east boundary or rim of the feature.

12.3.name: West Part
12.3.description: The flag is inside the western part of a larger feature.

12.4.name: East Corner — Inside
12.4.description: The flag is inside the corner whose point faces east.

12.5.name: South Corner — Outside
12.5.description: The flag is outside the corner whose point faces south.

12.6.name: South West Tip
12.6.description: The flag is at the narrow, south-west-pointing tip of the feature.

12.7.name: North West End
12.7.description: The flag is at the north-west end of a linear feature.

12.8.name: Upper part
12.8.description: The flag is near the upper end of a feature extending up a slope.

12.9.name: Lower part
12.9.description: The flag is near the lower end of a feature extending down a slope.

12.10.name: Top
12.10.description: The flag is on top of the feature, or on the upper of two levels.

12.11.name: Foot
12.11.description: The flag is where the slope of the feature meets the surrounding ground.

12.12.name: North East Foot
12.12.description: The flag is at the north-east foot of a feature with several possible foot positions.

12.13.name: Beneath
12.13.description: The flag is below the feature, or on the lower of two levels.

12.14.name: Between
12.14.description: The flag lies between two features identified separately in columns D and E.

13.1.name: First Aid post
13.1.description: First aid is available at this control.

13.2.name: Refreshment point
13.2.description: Refreshments are available at this control.

13.3.name: Manned control
13.3.description: An official is present at this control.

15.6.name: Map Flip
15.6.description: Turn the map over to continue on its other side.
